title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving WASH assistance to vulnerable communities affected by climate related shocks in Buaale District.

description.narrative: ltpgtInadequate and poor access to water sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services exacerbated by continued restrictions of access to the Humanitarian actors for more than a decade remain among the biggest threats to lives of the populations of Buale District who are streaming into Government controlled districts of Afmadow, Dhoble and Kismaayo of Lower Juba due to extended climate related shocks and conflicts. The communities also face the spill overs of problems facing the Villages due to strained capacities of existing WASH resource occasioned by lack of infrastructure development and maintenance of existing WASH infrastructure. Through this action, Jubba Foundation envisions to increase sustainable access to safe water, sanitation facilities and improved hygiene practices among ltbrgt16,921( 5,034 women, 3,764 girls, 4,693 men, and 3,430 boys) climate related shocks affected populations living in Buale town,Sukela, Anole, Banta, Bula Galole and Waraha Dhobley Settlements in Buale District, Somalia.ltbrgt Juba Foundation will undertake Drilling of one (1) borehole to improve access to clean water for 5,000 individuals as per WASH cluster standards . In addition, three water kiosk will be constructed and linked to borehole through an extension pipeline to serve Villages and settlements. The project will also improve access to safe sanitation facilities through construction of 26 culturally appropriate, disability friendly and gender segregated latrines targeting 600 individuals in Bant, Bula Galole and Waraha Dhobley Settlements . To enhance safe sanitation practices, the project will engage 15 (9 male and 6 female) community hygiene promoters (CHP) to conduct hygiene promotion campaigns focusing on hand washing with soap. To ensure sustainability of the water access and continued uptake of handwashing practices to promote hygiene practices, Jubba Foundation will conduct capacity building to the selected 15 CHPs and training 15 (9 male and 6 female) water management committees’ members on operation and maintenance of the established water kiosks. The project will adopt a market-based programme (MBP) approach to deliver essential WASH goods and services by utilizing the functional market in Buale District which also act as the business hub for the District to provide relief and basic services through purchase of goods in the local market, source of local contractors and supporting demand through vouchers. The MPB approach will therefore ensure appropriateness and dignity by allowing targeted affected populations to purchase according to their needs and preferences and improve efficiency of programme delivery by using existing supply chains can be cost-effective, reduce duplication and provide supplies quicker through market actors who are already present. Through close coordination with WASH and protection clusters, the project will contribute to an integrated and accountable response that meets immediate humanitarian needs while laying the foundation for more resilient, inclusive services in Buale District.ltbrgtlt/pgt
